themes_detail.label: Street noise surge THIS WEEK
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints in Forest Hills/Rego Park exploded to 28 reports THIS WEEK—a 339% spike compared to the 6.4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.69)—suggesting a sudden, localized disruption affecting outdoor public spaces.
evidence: 28 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.4-complaint 8-week baseline (339% increase, z-score 9.69)
Highest statistical severity among all current spikes in the district
Pattern is acute and recent, not chronic—suggests specific source or event rather than systemic issue
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden noise surge this week? Interview residents on affected blocks and check for construction, demolition, or special events.
Map the 28 complaints geographically to pinpoint epicenter—is it concentrated on one avenue (e.g., Queens Boulevard, Yellowstone Boulevard) or dispersed across the district?

themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints in Forest Hills/Rego Park spiked to 15 reports LAST WEEK—a 243% increase over the 4.4-complaint 8-week average (z-score: 4.26)—indicating a possible pest outbreak or sanitation failure affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: 15 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.4-complaint 8-week baseline (243% increase, z-score 4.26)
Coincides with elevated dead animal complaints (11 LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 average, 1000% spike, z-score 8.94)
Two-vector pest signal suggests environmental failure—possible garbage accumulation, unsealed buildings, or decline in rodent control services
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation and Parks officials: Has there been a service gap or staffing shortage affecting trash collection or pest control in the past 2-3 weeks?
Speak with residents and building superintendents on blocks with multiple complaints to identify common thread (e.g., new construction, blocked drain, nearby demolition site).

themes_detail.label: Dead animal cleanup backlog
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints surged to 11 reports LAST WEEK—a 1000% spike over the 1.0-complaint 8-week average (z-score: 8.94)—suggesting Parks or Sanitation is unable to respond to carcass removal in a timely manner.
evidence: 11 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0-complaint 8-week baseline (1000% increase, z-score 8.94)
Overlaps with rodent spike (15 complaints LAST WEEK), indicating dual pest/sanitation crisis
Related to recurring CB budget request for DEP capital spending, suggesting long-standing infrastructure gap
reporting_angles: Check 311 response times: Are carcasses sitting on streets for multiple days? Request Parks Department response data.
Investigate whether staffing cuts or route changes have impacted dead animal removal frequency in this district.

themes_detail.label: Residential noise sustained surge
themes_detail.summary: Residential noise complaints peaked at 63 reports TWO WEEKS AGO—a 414% spike over the 12.2-complaint 8-week average (z-score: 8.38)—indicating acute disruption to indoor quiet in homes, though intensity may be declining this week.
evidence: 63 residential noise complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 12.2-complaint 8-week baseline (414% increase, z-score 8.38)
Combined with street noise spike THIS WEEK (28 complaints vs. 6.4 average), suggests sustained noise crisis across indoor and outdoor environments
Four active ULURP rezonings in pipeline (Yellowstone Boulevard, Queens Boulevard, 108th Street, 68th Road) may be driving construction-related disruption
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 noise complaints with active building permits (274 filings in last 90 days, mostly alterations) to determine if construction is primary driver.
Interview residents in buildings near Yellowstone Boulevard and Queens Boulevard rezoning sites—are they experiencing noise from demolition or prep work?

themes_detail.label: Overgrown vegetation and hazard trees
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints jumped to 5 reports TWO WEEKS AGO—a 400% spike over the 1.0-complaint 8-week average (z-score: 3.58)—suggesting Parks Department is deferring tree maintenance, creating pedestrian and property hazards.
evidence: 5 overgrown tree/branch complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 1.0-complaint 8-week baseline (400% increase, z-score 3.58)
Recurring CB budget request for 'park or amenity expansion' suggests district residents prioritize green space maintenance
Possible indicator of Parks budget strain or deferred maintenance in low-priority residential blocks
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department: What is the current tree-trimming backlog in CD 406? Have staffing or budget cuts delayed routine maintenance?
Photograph overgrown hazard trees affecting sidewalk access or sightlines—document specific locations for story
